Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Title: Weapon Poses
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Text:
The game keeps a single weapon-drawn pose for all jobs. This tweak remembers one for each job.

To save a pose: draw your weapon and use /cpose until you like it. It is saved for your current job automatically.

When you switch to a job with a saved pose, it is put back as soon as you draw your weapon outside of combat.

"Default" means no pose has been saved for that job yet.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Name: GoblinSniper
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Description: Watches the market board for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for (like a mount listed at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000) and lists them. The number of deals found shows in the Server Info Bar.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Language.Help: Language of the item names in the window and in the search below. Independent of the GoblinTweaks language; defaults to it.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify: Show in the Server Info Bar
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify.Help: Adds an entry with the number of deals found. Click it to open the window.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.WholeDataCenter.Help: Looks at every world of your data center, not only your home world. You have to visit the world to buy.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Discount.Help: A listing must be at least this far below the normal price, and below the next seller.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MinPrice.Help: Items that normally sell for less than this are ignored.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxAge.Help: Ignores listings whose price was uploaded longer ago than this. Lower means fewer deals, but more reliable ones.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxDays.Help: Ignores items nobody has bought in more than this many days: they would just sit on the market.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Types.Help: Every marketable item of the chosen types is watched. The number is how many items each type adds. The big types (weapons, armor, furnishings) make each scan take a few minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Items.Help: Watch individual items of any type. Search by name and click a result to add it.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Sort.Name: Name

Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Title: What it does
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Text:
GoblinSniper looks for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for. Most of the time the seller made a typo: a mount listed at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000.

A listing counts as a deal only if all of this is true:

- It is below the average price by at least the discount you chose.
- It is also that far below the next seller. If everyone lists low, the price simply dropped.
- The item normally sells for more than your minimum price.
- The data is not older than your maximum data age.
- Someone bought the item recently (within 60 days by default).

With a low discount (30%) you will mostly see price differences between worlds. Raise it to keep only real mistakes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Title: Columns
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Text:
Item: icon, name and type. Hover a row to see the game's tooltip. Click a row to copy the item name, then paste it in the search of a market board.

iLvl: the item level.

Avg. price: the average sale price over the last few days in the area being scanned. If the item rarely sells, the price of its last sale is used.

Listed price: the cheapest listing right now, in green. Below it, "Next" is the cheapest listing from a different seller.

Discount: how far the listed price is below the average price.

World: where the listing is. To buy it, you have to travel to that world.

Updated: how long ago that price was uploaded.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Title: Resale chance
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Text:
The Resale column estimates how likely you are to sell the item again on your home world within 7 days.

It comes from "sales per day", a figure Universalis calculates from the last few days of sales and shows under the percentage. At 0.1 sales per day (one every 10 days) the chance is about 50%; at 0.5 per day it is about 97%.

Green is 75% or more, yellow is 40% or more, red is less.

If your world has no recent sales, an even share of the whole data center's sales is used instead.

It is only an estimate: it assumes you list at a price people will pay, and it does not know how many other sellers you compete with.

Items nobody has bought for too long are left out of the list: 60 days by default, see "Maximum days without a sale" in the settings. Universalis does not say how long a listing has been up, so this is judged by the last sale of the item.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Title: Sorting and filters
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Text:
"Sort by" only changes the order of the list: biggest discount (in %), biggest saving (in gil), lowest price, highest avg. price, item level, name, item type, world, or most recently updated.

The two lists next to it are filters, and they do hide rows:

- World: only the deals of one world. It lists the worlds that have a deal right now.
- Data age: only the deals whose price was uploaded less than 1, 3, 6 or 12 hours ago.

The search box filters by item name or world name.

The small X next to the search box clears it. The round arrow next to the filters resets them to all worlds and any data age.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Title: Prices and data age
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Text:
The game cannot show you the market board of another world, so prices come from Universalis, a public site that players feed when they open an item on a market board.

That is why data has an age. "Updated: 15h" means nobody has looked at that item on that world for 15 hours, so the listing may already be sold.

The plugin cannot make the data newer, but you can: travel to that world and open the item on the market board, and it is uploaded right away.

Popular items are refreshed all the time. Rare ones can go many hours without an update.

To see only recent data, lower "Maximum data age" in the settings. You will get fewer deals, but more reliable ones.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Title: Scans and alerts
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Text:
A scan runs shortly after you log in, every few minutes (see the settings), when you change a setting, and when you press the scan button (the arrows, top right). The gear next to it opens the settings.

Deals appear as they are found, without waiting for the scan to end. A deal from the previous scan stays listed until its item is checked again.

The scan button is locked until the scan ends, so a scan cannot be started twice. The bottom bar shows the progress.

The number in the Server Info Bar is how many deals are on the list right now. Click it to open this window, or hover to see the best ones.

If the bottom bar says Universalis is overloaded or did not answer, nothing is wrong on your side. What was found is kept, and the scan is retried in a couple of minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Title: Which items are watched
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Text:
Only what you choose in the settings is scanned, not the whole game. "Items watched" in the bottom bar is that total.

Item types: mounts, minions, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards, bardings, fashion accessories, hairstyles and emotes, dyes, materia, workshop parts, other collectibles, weapons, armor and furnishings. Each shows how many items it adds.

Weapons, armor and furnishings have thousands of items, so a scan that includes them takes a few minutes.

Specific items: search for any item by name in the settings and click it to watch it, whatever its type.

Only items that can be sold on the market board are included. The language of the item names is chosen in the settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Name: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Description: Shows the damage and healing you deal and take around the center of the screen, where your character stands, instead of over the target. It also announces buffs, debuffs and cooldowns. Events, areas, colors and the order of each message are all configurable. Type /gbt in chat to open its settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Open.Help: Opens the settings window. Sample text scrolls while it is open.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Title: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Positionals:
Some actions hit harder from the rear or the flank of the target (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet, Gallows, Fang and Claw...). This tweak tells you whether you hit that positional. Which actions have one, and on which side, is read from the game's own description of each action, so there is no list to keep up to date.

The game never says whether you hit it, so it is worked out from two things:
- The bonus. Each hit reports how much of its potency is bonus (combo plus positional). The potencies in the action's description, at your level (synced or not), tell what the bonus is with the positional and without it.
- Where you stood. The rear is the quarter of the circle behind the enemy, 45° to each side of its back. The flanks are the two quarters at its sides.

The verdict:
- No bonus at all: missed.
- Action with no combo (Gibbet, Trick Attack...): any bonus is the positional, so hit.
- The bonus of a hit: hit.
- The bonus of a miss, or an unexpected one (an effect is raising the potency): where you stood decides.

True North, enemies with no sides and effects that remove positionals count as hit, as in the game. Actions that deal no damage say nothing.

Turn it on, choose its area, or show it in the damage message in the Events tab. Its look is in the Highlights tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.OverTime.Te:
The game sends damage over time (DoT) and healing over time (HoT) ticks with no action attached: one number per target every 3 seconds.

Name and icon: those of the effect that ticks, like 132 Higanbana or +78 Regen. If several effects tick, all are named, and so are effects on the ground, like Doton. If none is found, the tick just says (DoT) or (HoT).

Whose tick it is:
- Sometimes the game says who applied it (healing over time, ground effects). Then you only see yours and your pet's, and the number is exact.
- Usually it does not (most damage over time). The game sends one sum of everyone's damage on that enemy. If none of it is yours, nothing is shown. If only yours is there, the number is exact. If others are on the enemy too, your share is an estimate, split by effect and marked with ~, like ~178 Higanbana.

Where it appears:
- Healing over time on you counts as healing received, whoever gave it.
- On anyone else (your pet included) it counts as healing given, and only shows if you or your pet gave it.
- Damage over time on you counts as damage taken.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Title: What counts as yours
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Text:
Debuffs on enemies: only yours. You see + name when it starts and - name when it ends. The same debuff from another player of your job is told apart. Nothing is shown when the enemy dies.

Pets: with Include my pet and chocobo (General tab), whatever your pet or chocobo deals, heals or applies to others counts as yours, including when it heals itself.

Counterattacks: when an effect like Vengeance or Damnation hits back, the message shows the name and icon of that action instead of a plain Attack.

Auto-attacks: when they are not yours, they say who made them, like Attack Kweh, or the name of the enemy hitting you. Actions of your pet or chocobo also end with its name.

Merged hits: with the Merge options (General tab), an action that hits several targets shows one total and the number of hits. Hits merge only with hits of the same kind: normal with normal, direct with direct, critical with critical and critical direct with critical direct.

Effects that fail: if an enemy is immune to the effect of your action, or fully resists it, the action says so after its name, like Leg Sweep Immune, in the miss color. It appears where actions with no damage appear.

Actions with no damage: an action of your job that deals no damage and heals nothing shows its icon and name, like a dash or a stun such as Leg Sweep. If it only puts an effect on you, that effect is announced instead.

Effects like Bloodbath: what an attack heals you for counts as healing received.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.PositionalInline: Shows whether you hit the positional in the damage message, after the action name, instead of in a separate alert. The area and movement set for the positional alert then do not apply: it appears where the damage does.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Positional: Shows whether you hit the positional of an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank. Choose its area and movement here, or show it in the damage message with the option below. Its look is in the Highlights tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Positi: Gives the alert for a positional you hit its own look. Off: it uses its area's font and size, in green.
Gives the alert for a positional you missed its own look. Off: it uses its area's font and size, in red.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Gradie: Blends the text from the alert color to a second color.
Whether the gradient goes from left to right or from top to bottom.
The color the gradient ends on.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHeals.Help: An action that heals several targets at once shows one total with the number of heals. Off: one message per target.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowHealTargets: Show who my healing is for
Heals you give end with the name of who they heal, in brackets. Merged heals have several targets and name none: turn off Merge healing on several targets to see each name.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.ActionUsed: An action of your job that deals no damage, heals nothing and applies no effect, like a dash. The game shows no text for these.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Star: Left: messages start at the area position and grow to the right.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Midd: Center: messages are centered on the area position.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.End: Right: messages end at the area position and grow to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: Kind of animation. Choosing one lists its animations on the right and plays the first.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Hint: Click to turn on or off. Lit: announced. Hover for the name.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Colors.Help: One color per kind of text. Click a color to open the color picker.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.None: No event is sent to this area. Choose where each event goes in the Events tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Preview.Hint: Sample text is on. Drag each area's box to move it. Press ? for help.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHits.Help: An attack that hits several targets at once shows a single total with the number of hits.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeMisses.Help: Misses, dodges and invulnerable hits of one action show as one message with the number of times, like Miss x3. Off: one message each.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeDefended.He: Blocked, parried and resisted hits of one action merge, each kind with its own kind. Off: they show one by one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeNoEffect.He: An effect that fails on several targets of one action shows once with the number of times, like Leg Sweep Immune x3. Off: one message each.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeTicks: Merge damage and healing over time
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeTicks.Help: The ticks of one effect on several targets, like your Higanbana on three enemies, show as one message with the number of ticks, like 132 Higanbana x3. Off: one message per tick.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.IncludePets.Help: What your pet or chocobo deals is shown as outgoing.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowDefended.Hel: Damage that was blocked, parried or resisted says so after the number, like -270 (parried). Off: only the number shows.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Mitigation.Help: Adds how much of the damage you take was removed by your damage reduction. Percent only: -270 (-30%). With the word: -270 (-30% mitigated). It is worked out from the effects active at that moment, using the percentages in the descriptions of the actions that give them.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Font.Help: Font of every message. Size is set per area, in the Areas tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Enabled.Hel: Off: these events use the game's own floating text.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetX.Hel: Pixels to the right (positive) or left (negative) of the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetY.Hel: Pixels below (positive) or above (negative) the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Help: Which point of each message sits on the area position. 0: the message starts there and grows to the right. 50: centered. 100: it ends there and grows to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Height.Help: Pixels a message travels before it disappears.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.FontSize.He: Text size for this area. Highlighted messages (special hits, cooldown alerts) have their own size, set in the Highlights and Cooldowns tabs.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Duration.He: Seconds a message stays on screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MinAmount.H: Damage and healing below this amount is hidden, both here and in the game's own text. 0 shows everything.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Style.Help: Path of this area's messages: straight, curved to one side, or Static (they stay in place, fade, and pile up as more arrive).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order: Order of each message in this area
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.Help: Left-to-right order of the parts of a message in this area. Arrows move a part; the eye hides or shows it. Only parts used by events sent to this area are listed. Each area has its own order.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Part.Name: Action name
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowFading.Help: Buffs and debuffs are announced when they end (- name) as well as when they start (+ name).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Area.Help: Where this event appears: Outgoing (right of your character), Incoming (left) or Center (below).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageDeal: Damage you, your pet or your damage over time deal, with misses.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageTake: Damage you receive, with what you dodge.
Healing you receive, from yourself or from others.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Mp.Help: MP you recover from actions and effects.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnMe.H: A beneficial effect starts or ends on you, whoever gave it.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnOthe: A beneficial effect you put on someone else starts.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnMe: A harmful effect starts or ends on you.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnEn: A harmful effect of yours starts or ends on an enemy.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Cooldown.H: Announces when one of the actions ticked below is ready to use again.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Help: Click an action to turn its alert on or off. Lit: announced. Dimmed: not. The list is for the job you had when this window opened.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.None: No actions with a cooldown found. Log in on a combat job and reopen this window.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Goblin Battle Text settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Motion.Hel: How this event moves: up, down or Static (stays in place and fades). If an area's path is Static, all its events stay still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.CooldownOrder.He: Left to right order of the parts of a cooldown alert. The eye hides or shows a part.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Overview.Te:
Goblin Battle Text replaces the numbers that float over the target with text around the center of the screen, where your character stands, so you never lose sight of it. The game's own numbers for those events are hidden, so nothing shows twice.

There are three areas:
- Outgoing, right of your character: what you do.
- Incoming, left: what happens to you.
- Center, below: effects that start or end, and cooldowns.

Each kind of event can go to any area, or be turned off.

Open this window with /gbt or from the tweak card in GoblinTweaks. While it is open, sample text scrolls so you can see each change at once, and each area has a named box you can drag to move it. Settings save automatically and are per character: a character seen for the first time starts with a copy of your current settings. The name under this window's title says whose settings you are editing.

Hold the button at the bottom right to reset the tab you are looking at to its defaults.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.General.Tex:
Merge damage / healing on several targets: an area attack or heal shows one total with the number of hits. Each has its own switch.

Show who my healing is for: heals you give end with the name of who they heal, unless they are merged.

Damage and healing over time: the game sends one tick per target with everyone's damage added up. When others also have effects on that target, yours is shown as an estimate, with ~ before it.

Shorten large numbers: 12.3K instead of 12,345.

Include my pet and chocobo: their damage counts as yours.

Show blocked, parried and resisted: whether such hits say so after the number.

Mitigated: adds how much of the damage you take was removed, as a percent only, like -270 (-30%), or with the word, like -270 (-30% mitigated). It counts effects on you that reduce damage (Rampart, Damnation, Kerachole...) and effects on the attacker that lower its damage (Reprisal, Feint, Addle...), each with the percent in its action's description. Several multiply, as in the game. Blocks, parries, barriers and anything without a percent in its description are not counted.

Font: the font of every message. Size is set per area, in the Areas tab.

Colors: one per kind of text: damage dealt, damage taken, healing, misses and dodges, MP gained, actions with no damage, and buffs and debuffs (one color when they start, another when they end). Click a color to open the picker: Confirm applies it, Default restores the original, Cancel leaves it as it was.

The colors of critical and direct hits are in the Highlights tab; those of the cooldown alert are in the Cooldowns tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Title: Areas tab
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Text:
Choose the area at the top: Outgoing, Incoming or Center. All three have the same settings. The Restore button only affects the one you are looking at, and the cog next to the switch copies this area's look to another.

Show this area: off, its events go back to the game's own text.

Position X and Y: where the area is, in pixels from the center of the screen (negative is left or up). Drag the area's box on screen, move the slider, or type the exact number with + and -.

Alignment: 0, messages start at the area position and grow to the right. 50, centered. 100, they end there and grow to the left. The three buttons set those values.

Scroll distance, Font size and Duration (in seconds).

Minimum amount: smaller damage and healing is not shown.

Messages at once: how many show at the same time, 1 to 15. When another arrives, the oldest disappears.

Path: straight, curved to one side, or Static (messages stay in place and fade).

Order of each message: arrows move a part earlier or later; the eye hides or shows it. Only parts used by events sent to this area are listed.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Events.Text:
One row per kind of event, with three settings:

- The checkbox turns the event on or off. Off, the game shows it as usual.
- Area: Outgoing, Incoming or Center.
- Movement: up, down or Static.

Events: Damage dealt and Damage taken (with misses and dodges), Healing on allies, Healing received (including what effects like Bloodbath heal you for), MP gained, Buff on me, Debuff on me, Buff I give, Debuff on enemy, and Action with no damage (dashes and other actions the game shows no text for).

Announce effects that end: buffs and debuffs show + name when they start and - name when they wear off.

Messages never cross. When an area has events going up and events going down, each direction gets half of the area and starts from its middle. Static events pile up just outside the scrolling path. If the halves feel short, raise the area's scroll distance.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Cooldowns.T:
Cooldown alerts tell you when an action is ready again, like "Fast Blade ready now!". They are off until you tick the checkbox at the top. Next to it you choose the area and how the alert moves.

Own look for the alert: font, size, animation, intensity and the color of the "ready now!" text. Off, the alert uses its area's font and size, in white. The action name always has its own color.

Order of the cooldown alert: its three parts (icon, action name, "ready now!" text). Arrows move a part; the eye hides it.

Actions of your current job: click one to turn its alert on or off (lit: announced). Hover to see its name, or type part of it in the search box.

Which actions are listed: those of your job, at your level, with their own cooldown of 5 seconds or more (not the global one). Actions that share a cooldown, like an action and its upgrade, count once. The alert comes when the cooldown ends; with charges, when all of them are back. The list is for the job you had when the window opened: after changing job, close and reopen it.

Procs are not listed. An effect that makes an action available shows as Buff on me.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Defaults.Help: Hold down to reset every setting of the current tab to its default. In the Areas tab, only the current area is reset. Other tabs are not touched.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical hits (marked with !) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Direct: Gives direct hits their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical direct hits (marked with !!) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Cooldo: Gives cooldown alerts their own look. Off: they use their area's font and size, with white text.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Font.H: Font of this kind of message, in place of the general one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: What the message does when it appears: choose the kind first, then the animation. There are 35; the sample text plays the one you pick, so try a few.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.FontSi: Size of this kind of message, in place of that of its area.
Choose at the top what to set: critical hits (!), direct hits, critical direct hits (!!), and the alerts for a positional you hit or missed. Each has its own look. The look of the cooldown alert is in the Cooldowns tab.

Positional alerts: when you use an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet...), an alert says whether you hit it from there. True North counts as a hit. Turn them on or off, and choose their area, in the Events tab.

- Checkbox: off, the message looks like any other in its area.
- Colors: one for damage you deal and one for damage you take. Critical hits have a third for healing, the only other thing that can be critical.
- Gradient (positional alerts): blends the text from its color to a second one, left to right or top to bottom.
- Font and Font size, instead of the area's.
- Animation, played when the message appears: pick its kind in the first list and the animation in the second.
- Intensity: strength of the animation, 0 to 300; 100 is normal.

Gentle: Pop, Shake, Pulse, Flash.
Impacts: Slam, Quake, Earthquake, Stomp, Crush, Shockwave, Meteor, Fury.
Size: Bounce, Zoom, Stretch, Explode, Heartbeat.
Rotation: Swing, Rattle, Spin, Tornado.
Movement: Drop, Launch, Dash, Recoil.
Light: Blaze, Thunder, Ignite, Ember, Frost, Venom, Blood, Radiance, Shadow, Strobe.

While this tab is open, the sample text only shows the kind chosen at the top.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Intens: Strength of the animation in percent: how much it grows, how far it moves or tilts, how bright or dark it gets. 100 is normal, 0 leaves the message still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MaxMessages: How many messages this area shows at once, 1 to 15. When another arrives, the oldest disappears.
